 US aviation authority grounds all departing flights, citing communication issues
 By Luke Cooper , Scout Wallen , Elissa Fitzgerald , Angela Lavoipierre and Brad Ryan in Washington DC Topic: Air Incidents
 Posted Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:12am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:12am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:12am Airplanes are grounded across the US. ( Reuters: Jonathan Ernst ) 
 Skip to timeline abc.net.au/news/follow-live-us-aviation-authority-grounds-all-flights/107385742 Link copied Share Share article All departing flights across the US have been grounded after a national halt order was issued by the nation's aviation regulator.
 The Federal Aviation Administration says a communication issue has affected all air route traffic control centres.
 Follow our live coverage.
 Submit a comment or question 
 Log in to comment Live updates
 Recap
 Here is a summary of key events so far:
 The US Federal Aviation Administration has issued a national ground stop for all departing flights   "due to extraordinary circumstance and reasons for safety" .
 The US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed the order was   given due to a communication issue affecting all air route traffic control centres .
 US Homeland Security Secretary   Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication that a nefarious act was behind the issue.
 The halt order is just the second ground stop issued by flight regulators since the September 11 terror attacks in 2001.

 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:32am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:32am US weather service now working
 S By Scout Wallen
 Earlier, we said the   US National Weather Service was currently experiencing   nationwide internet and communications problems. 
 That radar issue is now resolved, and the website is fully operational.
 Reporting with Reuters 
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:27am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:27am A deeper look into whether AI tool may have sparked nationwide flight disruption
 A By Angela Lavoipierre
 There are questions as to whether the recent nationwide rollout of a new AI air traffic tool known as " SMART"   could be behind the disruptions, so I’ve taken a closer look at it.
 The tool was rolled out on November 10 , several days ago, with no obvious issues – or at least none on this scale.
 Still, it’s worth mentioning that 25 Democrat members of Congress wrote a letter to the US Transport Secretary Sean Duffy last month, raising significant concerns about the rollout, including a lack of adequate testing and the risk of hallucinations.
 “We are deeply concerned about the integration of any AI-enabled system into air traffic control systems, where decisions are literally a matter of life or death”, they wrote.
 A short time ago, the company behind the tool, Air Space Intelligence , posted on X , denying any link: "The current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC."
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:23am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:23am 📽️: Homeland Security Secretary says there is no safety threat
 S By Scout Wallen
 Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin addressed the media a short time ago.
 He says authorities   don't know yet   if a cyber attack is behind the incident , but has assured Americans that no one is in danger.   
 Loading... Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:20am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:20am Are flights still in the air?
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 Flight Radar 24 shows flights as normal!
 - Mark 
 Hi Mark,
 The national halt is only affecting planes still on the ground, with those already in the air allowed to complete their journeys.
 So, the longer the ground stop continues, the fewer planes we'll see in the air.
 The traffic outside Dulles International Airport in Virginia. (Reuters: Daniel Heuer) Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:12am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:12am Flights may be grounded, but Elon Musk has launched a rocket
 S By Scout Wallen
 While planes are grounded across the US, one take-off has been allowed to go ahead.
 A short time ago, SpaceX   launched its 15th Starship rocket flight from Texas on a mission to complete the first round-trip voyage, to orbit out and back to the very spot where it left Earth .
 It is carrying a batch of Starlink satellites, meaning it's a money-making endeavour for Elon Musk , as well as a high-stakes test for a rocket ship still under development.
 The 15th Starship launched from Texas. (AP: Eric Gay) Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:08am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:08am The latest from the FAA
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 The US Federal Aviation Administration says the nationwide ground stop remains in effect.  
 It adds that as enroute facilities recover, flights will be allowed to depart through coordination with the air traffic control system command centre.
 Reporting with Reuters 
 Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:06am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 10:06am How many flights have been delayed or cancelled?
 L By Luke Cooper
 Given this is an unfolding situation right across the United States , the numbers are still in flux.
 But, what we can tell you so far is that the nationwide ground halt order appears to be impacting tens of thousands of travellers in the US.
 FlightAware , an online aircraft tracking website, is reporting that around 10,500 flights into and out of the US have already been delayed today.
 The website also says that more than 1,800 flight services have been cancelled .
 As a reminder, it's just ticked past 6pm local time in the US's eastern states and 3pm in western cities such as Los Angeles .
 Some major airlines have also flagged they are expecting this disruption to persist for some time yet.
 Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:59am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:59am Radars and radio frequencies also affected: CNN
 S By Scout Wallen
 CNN is reporting the nationwide flights disruption is also affecting   air traffic control radars and radio frequencies .
 CNN says it spoke to a source familiar with what controllers are dealing with, who told them that controllers do not have any clarity on the cause and what exactly is going on.
 The   US National Weather Service is also currently experiencing   nationwide internet and communications problems. 
 This could be preventing people from accessing services on its website.
 There is no evidence that the incidents are linked.   
 Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:57am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:57am Is the US flight disruption linked to Microsoft outage or AI tool rollout?
 A By Angela Lavoipierre
 Speculation is rife on social media about a possible connection between the 21-hour Microsoft outage, which was resolved this morning, and the US flight disruptions.
 However, US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters: "I don’t see any reason to connect those two at all." 
 Separately, he was asked about reports that the FAA was due to roll out its new artificial intelligence-based air traffic tool today, and whether that could be the reason for the comms outage.
 He said: "We’re looking at that."
 Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:54am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:54am Telco responsible for FAA's tech systems 'not aware of issue'
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 US telco Verizon says its network is "fully functioning", and   it is not aware of any issue related to air traffic control systems.   
 The US Federal Aviation Administration awarded Verizon a 15-year contract potentially worth $US2.4 billion ($3.5 billion) to upgrade the agency's technology systems.
 FAA technicians are currently investigating the cause of the communications failure.
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:46am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:46am 📽️: Footage shows grounded flights in LA
 S By Scout Wallen
 The   Los Angeles International Airport would normally be a hub of activity on a Friday afternoon, but this footage shows a quieter scenario.
 Loading... Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:43am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:43am 'I will be demanding answers,' US senator says
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 US Senator Tammy Duckworth, the ranking member in the Senate's aviation subcommittee, has called for a "thorough and complete" investigation into the ground stop.
 "Whatever led to the nationwide ground stop will warrant a thorough and complete investigation," she wrote on X.
 "As Aviation Subcommittee Ranking Member, I'll be demanding answers from the FAA."
 Loading Twitter content Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:39am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:39am 📷: What it's like inside US airports right now
 S By Scout Wallen
 This flight shutdown began on Friday afternoon , local time, when many Americans would have been commuting for the weekend.
 A reminder that there has been no update as to when the order will be lifted. 
 Here's what it looks like inside some US airports right now.
 People stand in line at John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York. (Reuters: Angelina Katsanis) Commuters are waiting in airports aross the country. (Getty Images via AFP: Finn Gomez) Flights are being delayed across the country. (AP: Ethan Swope) Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:38am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:38am How long the US's biggest airlines expect disruption to last
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
 American Airlines has told customers disruptions are likely "for the rest of the day", depending on the duration of the nationwide grounding.
 "It will be all hands on deck across American to get customers on their way as soon as possible when the FAA lifts this ground stop," a statement reads.
 It is just past 5.30pm in New York and 2.30pm in Los Angeles.   
 Loading Twitter content Another of the country's largest carriers, United Airlines , has also issued its own statement addressing the disruptions.
 "United flights that are already airborne will continue," the company says.
 "New domestic flights will not depart while the FAA ground stop remains in place.
 "United will work with our customers to get them to their destinations once this issue is resolved."
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:30am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:30am Flights can land safely, says Mullin
 B By Brad Ryan in Washington DC
   Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin   says not all communications are down, and he has stressed that flights in the air right now would be able to land safely.
 "We are able to communicate at certain levels, but it's overwhelmed some of the systems we have," he said.
 " We're assured that everybody is safe.
 "Everybody that's going to be in the air, that's currently on a plane, your loved ones, as I said, we're going to get you on the ground, and we're doing it in a safe manner."
 US Homeland Security Secretary Markmwayne Mullin. (Reuters: Elizabeth Frantz) Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:29am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:29am The latest from the FAA
 E By Elissa Fitzgerald
   The   US Federal Aviation Administration says flights have been grounded due to a temporary telecommunications outage.   
 "Out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted," the agency said in a statement.
 "Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case-by-case basis."
 Loading Twitter content Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:27am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:27am Flight Radar shows busy airspace
 S By Scout Wallen
 To give you an idea of just how busy the US's airspace is right now, here is a shot of the country from the FlightRadar24 website.
 The aircraft monitor shows hundreds of flights are still in the air over the country.
 As we've mentioned, the national halt order does not prevent those flights from landing, it will only impact planes still on the ground.
 Flight Radar shows the US airspace is busy. (Supplied: Flight Radar) Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:19am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:19am 'This isn't another 9/11,' Homeland Security Secretary says
 B By Brad Ryan in Washington DC
 US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has briefed reporters at the White House on the national ground stop.
 He said there was no threat to the public, but the root cause of the problem is not known.
 US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. (Reuters: Elizabeth Frantz) "There's no reason for the public to be afraid or scared for your loved ones," he said.
 "This isn't another 9/11.
 "This is a telecommunications outage. This is much different."
 Mullin could not say how long it would take for things to return to normal.
 "This isn't just going to be resolved and turned around within the hour," he said.
 He would not rule out a cyber attack, nor problems related to new AI-powered technology being rolled out in air control towers.
 US media is reporting that FBI and law enforcement sources do not believe the problem is the result of a cyber attack.
 Mr Mullin said there was also no reason to think yesterday's global Microsoft outage was linked to the issue.
 Key Event
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:14am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:14am What we know so far
 L By Luke Cooper
 The nationwide ground stop came after the FAA first halted traffic in Chicago due to air traffic control issues.
 The following order then stopped   "all departing traffic … until further notice". 
 The regulator says all international flights will be managed on a case-by-case basis.
 The order means flights already in the air may land but flights on the ground cannot take off.
 This is only the second nationwide ground stop in the United States since the September 11 terror attacks .
 The last one was in January 2023 , when domestic departures were paused for less than two hours.
 Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:08am Sat 14 Nov 2026 at 9:08am Flights grounded across the US
 L By Luke Cooper
 Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of the unfolding flight halt affecting all aircraft currently operating in the United States .
 The US Federal Aviation Administration has issued a national ground stop "due to extraordinary circumstance and reasons for safety". 
 It comes after the agency earlier reported serious air traffic control communications issues.
 My ABC colleagues and I will keep you up to date here with ongoing developments and information as it becomes available to us.
